hook.text: Your JavaScript tries to call another domain's API. The browser blocks it. CORS is why — and the fix.

buildup.text: Same-origin policy blocks cross-origin requests by default. It prevents a malicious page from stealing your data.

discovery.text: CORS lets servers opt in. The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header tells browsers which origins are allowed.

twist.text: Preflight OPTIONS requests check permission before the real request. The browser sends them automatically.

climax.text: Misconfigured CORS — like allowing all origins — undoes the entire security model. Be specific.

punchline.text: CORS controls cross-origin access. The server decides who's allowed.

quiz.question: What HTTP header does a server use to allow cross-origin requests?

details.summary: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing is a browser security mechanism that controls which websites can make requests to a different origin. Servers declare allowed origins, methods, and headers via CORS response headers.
details.whyItMatters: CORS protects users from malicious cross-site requests while enabling legitimate API access from different domains. Misconfigured CORS is one of the most common sources of web development frustration.
takeaways: Browsers block cross-origin requests unless the server permits them
Access-Control-Allow-Origin specifies which origins can access the API
Preflight OPTIONS requests check permissions for complex requests

faq.question: What triggers a CORS preflight request?
faq.answer: Browsers send a preflight OPTIONS request for non-simple requests: those using methods other than GET, HEAD, or POST, requests with custom headers, or POST requests with content types other than form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, or text/plain.

faq.question: How do you fix CORS errors?
faq.answer: Add Access-Control-Allow-Origin with the requesting origin to the API server's responses. For credentials, set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true with a specific origin — wildcards are not allowed with credentials. Set Access-Control-Allow-Methods and Allow-Headers for preflight requests.
